items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 registers ELDER_GUARDIAN (SimpleParticleType, wire id 24, overrideLimiter=true) with a dedicated ElderGuardianParticle$Provider (ParticleResources.registerProviders, 26.2 has its own ElderGuardianParticle class) and spawns it on game event GUARDIAN_ELDER_EFFECT (ClientPacketListener.handleGameEvent, addParticle at the player position, bytecode offset 536). The port's ParticleType enum (127 variants) lacks it, so received_particle drops server-sent elder_guardian packets (lan_particles.rs:482), /particle rejects it (particle.notFound, world_cmds.rs:770), and override_limiter() misses it (32 vanilla vs 31 Rust). Unlike 1.21.7, the 26.2 providers driver does NOT send elder_guardian cases (omitted from SIMPLE), so the defect blocks no driver here — it silently skips the type. The in-game curse apparition IS re-implemented via game event 10 + elder_apparition_geometry (30-tick lifetime, mob_blocks.rs:70/79), so the main visible path works through a different mechanism (fidelity unverified).
items.title: elder_guardian has no port implementation at all: no ParticleType variant, no engine provider, no limiter entry (recurs from 1.21.7)

items.evidence: Particle::read decodes wire id 49 (flash, verified against the 26.2 registry) as Color(i32) — a flash particle always carries a colour — but hub_particle has no Flash arm in its Color match (EntityEffect | TintedLeaves only, lan_particles.rs:431), so the packet is built with data None and Particle::write (writes data by presence, not id) emits the id with no colour bytes; guests reading id 49 consume the next 4 stream bytes as the colour and desync. Reachable only via /particle flash on a LAN host (cmd_particle builds ParticleOptions::simple(Flash), world_cmds.rs:881; Flash is otherwise created client-side only, in firework explosions, particles.rs:3739); the local player draws directly and is unaffected.
items.title: /particle minecraft:flash sends a malformed packet to LAN guests (recurs from 1.21.7)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 registers SPRUCE_LEAVES as TintedParticleLeavesBlock with leafParticleChance 0.01 (Blocks.class: BlockItemIds.SPRUCE_LEAVES -> lambda$static$27 -> TintedParticleLeavesBlock(0.01F); LeavesBlock.animateTick rolls nextFloat() < chance). The port maps spruce_leaves to Animate::Leaves(None, None) — no falling particle (animate_tick.rs:149). All 10 other leaf blocks match vanilla (cherry 0.1, pale oak 0.02, rest tinted 0.01; azalea fixed colour -9399763 matches exactly). The marker driver would fail its spruce zoo cases (oracle emits, probe emits none); the driver's own comment ('the spruce that never falls') encodes the same wrong belief and needs correcting with the fix.
items.title: Spruce leaves never drop falling-leaf particles (recurs from 1.21.7)

items.evidence: The port implements vibration end to end (Particle::read id 55, hub_particle arm, make() arm) and the providers oracle's options() handles it, but the providers driver's kind set never sends a vibration case, so the vibration provider's numerics have no driver coverage. Add vibration cases (target + duration) to test_particle_providers_parity.py.
items.title: Providers driver omits vibration: no driver coverage for the vibration provider

items.evidence: The providers driver's SIMPLE list carries red/orange/yellow_poplar_leaves, which are not in the 26.2 registry (26.3-only). The oracle resolves kinds by registry name and throws AssertionError('unknown particle ' + id) for an unregistered type (VanillaParticleProvidersOracle.java:131), so the driver cannot run against the 26.2 oracle as-is — it would die on the first poplar case (12 cases per kind). Trim the 3 kinds for 26.2.
items.title: Providers driver includes 3 poplar leaves (26.3-only); oracle throws on them against the 26.2 registry

items.evidence: The marker driver's zoo_states() sends red_poplar_leaves[distance=3,...] cases, but no such block exists in 26.2 (verified against registries.json) — the oracle cannot build that world. The port is correct to have no classify arm for it (26.2 has no poplar trees; animate_tick.rs:40-41). Trim the zoo case for 26.2.
items.title: Marker driver zoo includes red_poplar_leaves (26.3-only block)

systemic_note: Same shape as the 1.21.7 batch, with one 26.2 twist: the three defects are three different shapes — a missing registry entry carried through every table (B8-G01: one type absent from the enum, the limiter list, the command parser and the probe), a write-path/read-path asymmetry in one codec arm (B8-G02: the reader expects data the writer omits), and a wrong per-block belief baked into both the port and the driver's own comment (B8-G03: spruce). The 26.2 twist is that the drivers drifted toward the port instead of vanilla: the providers driver silently dropped elder_guardian from its kind set (so B8-G01 blocks nothing here, unlike 1.21.7 where it blocked the driver), while both drivers still carry 26.3-only poplar entries that cannot run against the 26.2 oracle (B8-H02, B8-H03). The positive systemic finding is that the port's particle tables are otherwise exact: all 125 types covered end-to-end except elder_guardian, all 22 data-carrying wire ids correct, all 32 limiter flags correct except elder_guardian, all 30 entity-burst pairs and all 42 real marker-zoo blocks covered, and all 11 leaf blocks' chances verified — the gaps are narrow and enumerated, not a broad drift. The 3 extra 26.3 types in the Rust enum (poplar leaves) are dead but unreachable.
